Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Molesworth (author, Wikidata Q6780145), died 1921; Walter Crane (illustrator, Wikidata Q660917), died 1915; Joseph Swain (illustrator, Wikidata Q16856885), died 1909. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Molesworth, Mrs., 1839-1921; Crane, Walter, 1845-1915 [Illustrator]; Swain, Joseph, 1820-1909 [Illustrator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Tell me a story and The adventures of Herr baby, New York, London, Macmillan and co., 1893, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/tellmestoryadven00mole. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 97%, 100%, 100% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Joseph Swain, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
